The role focuses on improving manufacturing efficiency, product quality and production performance through engineering analysis, process optimisation and continuous improvement while ensuring compliance with engineering specifications, quality standards and workplace safety requirements.   Benefits   Task & responsibilities   Duties:    Plan and improve manufacturing processes for the production of optical fibre current sensors, current transformers, transducers and related electrical products.  Analyse production processes and identify opportunities to improve productivity, product quality and manufacturing efficiency.  Prepare and maintain manufacturing documentation, including work instructions, standard operating procedures (SOPs) and process specifications.  Coordinate production activities to ensure products are manufactured on time and meet quality standards.  Investigate production issues, equipment faults and product defects, and implement corrective actions.  Monitor production performance and recommend process improvements to enhance efficiency and reduce waste.  Support the introduction of new products through production trials, process validation and manufacturing implementation.  Evaluate manufacturing equipment and recommend upgrades or process improvements to improve production performance.  Ensure manufacturing activities comply with engineering specifications, quality standards, workplace health and safety requirements and relevant Australian standards.  Work closely with Engineering, Quality, Production and Supply Chain teams to support continuous improvement and achieve production objectives.    Responsibilities:    Ensure manufacturing processes operate efficiently and achieve production and quality targets.  Maintain accurate engineering and production documentation.  Provide technical support to production staff and assist in resolving manufacturing issues.  Monitor product quality and ensure compliance with engineering specifications and company standards.  Identify opportunities for continuous improvement and implement practical engineering solutions.  Support equipment commissioning, process validation and engineering change implementation.  Ensure compliance with Workplace Health and Safety (WHS) policies and company procedures.  Collaborate with internal teams to support production planning and timely customer delivery.     Qualification & experience   Bachelor's degree or higher in Production Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.  Minimum of one (1) year of relevant full-time work experience as a Production Engineer or in a similar manufacturing engineering role.  Knowledge of manufacturing processes, production planning and process improvement.  Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings and technical specifications.  Understanding of quality management systems and workplace health and safety (WHS) requirements.  Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.  Good communication and teamwork skills.  Proficiency in Microsoft Office; experience with ERP/MRP systems or manufacturing software is an advantage.   About Company    Founded in Sydney in 2004, Smart Digital Optics (SDO) manufactures optical fibre current sensors for the electric power and smelting industries. Smart Digital Optics is one of the first companies to incorporate optical fibre current sensors into power monitoring and metering systems allowing users to measure electric currents with unprecedented levels of accuracy and ease. The digitally compatible and compact SDO products offer superior utility and performance compared to costly and cumbersome traditional approaches.  In 2010 SDO formed a strategic alliance with the Arteche Group. Arteche has 65 years of experience in the manufacture of electrical power products for generation, transmission, distribution and industrial applications. As an international benchmark with equipment in service in over 150 countries, it has companies in Europe, America, Asia and Oceania, as well as a service network comprised of more than 80 technical and sales offices.  The combination of SDO’s technology expertise with Arteche’s long experience in the electricity sector provides customers with a partner well equipped to support the introduce new technology for advanced transmission and industrial systems.   Technology :   SDO uses its expertise in advanced optics and signal processing to develop solutions for power engineering applications.  SDO’s optical current sensors utilize the Faraday effect in optical fibre, whereby the state of polarization of the light propagating in the fibre interacts with the magnetic field around a conductor.This effect is highly linear and provides the basis of an ultra high bandwidth, wide dynamic range current sensor which measures both AC and DC current with high accuracy. Universal Metal Fabrication is an established Australian metal fabrication business specialising in the design, manufacture, modification, repair, and servicing of custom truck bodies, transport equipment, and fabricated metal components. Operating from Campbellfield, Victoria, the business provides fabrication solutions to commercial transport operators and businesses requiring purpose-built vehicle bodies, structural modifications, repairs, and associated metal fabrication services.
The business undertakes a broad range of fabrication activities including structural steel fabrication, first-class welding, cutting, assembly, fitting, repairs, and the manufacture of custom truck bodies and specialised transport equipment. Operations involve interpreting engineering drawings, fabricating and assembling steel components, performing precision welding, and ensuring completed products meet Australian industry standards, quality requirements, and customer specifications.
Universal Metal Fabrication services clients across the transport, logistics, commercial, and industrial sectors, delivering custom fabrication solutions tailored to individual operational requirements. ABOUT THE ROLE
An opportunity exists for an experienced Welder (First Class) (ANZSCO 322313) to join the business on a full-time basis.

The successful candidate will be responsible for interpreting technical drawings, preparing materials, welding fabricated components, inspecting completed work, and supporting the efficient delivery of fabrication projects while maintaining high standards of workmanship and safety.
The position requires the ability to work independently and collaboratively within a fabrication team, maintain production quality, and contribute to the timely completion of engineering and fabrication projects.
This is a permanent full-time position based on a minimum 38-hour working week.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Fabrication Preparation and Material Processing
•	Interpret engineering drawings, blueprints, specifications, and work instructions to determine fabrication and welding requirements.
•	Select, inspect, clean, and prepare metal stock and fabricated components for welding.
•	Measure, mark, and cut steel, aluminium, stainless steel, and other metals using hand tools, flame cutting equipment, power tools, and metal cutting machinery.
•	Shape, bend, and prepare metal sections, pipes, and fabricated components using appropriate manual and mechanical techniques.
•	Prepare workpieces to ensure accurate fit-up prior to welding.

Welding and Fabrication
•	Align, position, and secure fabricated components using measuring equipment, clamps, jigs, and hand tools.
•	Perform welding using appropriate processes including MIG, TIG, Arc (MMAW), and other welding techniques where required.
•	Join metal components through welding, bolting, riveting, and related fabrication methods.
•	Manufacture, assemble, modify, and repair fabricated metal products in accordance with engineering specifications.
•	Complete fabrication work while maintaining dimensional accuracy, structural integrity, and quality standards.

Quality Assurance and Finishing
•	Inspect completed welds for penetration, bead profile, alignment, strength, and finish quality.
•	Identify and rectify welding defects or fabrication inconsistencies where required.
•	Finish fabricated products through grinding, filing, polishing, cleaning, and other finishing techniques.
